title: Monday.com vs Plane
comparison_markdown:
# Monday.com vs Plane (2026)

## Overview
Monday.com and Plane are both modern work management platforms designed to help teams track projects, manage tasks, and collaborate efficiently. This comparison benefits engineering managers, operations leads, and IT directors deciding between a hosted, all-in-one SaaS platform and an open-source, developer-centric alternative. Teams typically evaluate these options when looking to cut escalating per-user SaaS costs or seeking tighter control over their project management data and infrastructure.

## Key Differences
* **Cost:** Monday.com operates on a tiered SaaS subscription model ranging from $9 to $19+ per user per month, whereas Plane offers a free, open-source self-hosted edition alongside paid cloud tiers.
* **Data Ownership:** Monday.com stores all organizational data in their proprietary cloud environment, while Plane's self-hosted deployment keeps all source code, task data, and attachments entirely within your own private infrastructure.
* **Setup Complexity:** Monday.com requires zero installation time with instant account creation, whereas self-hosting Plane demands container management knowledge (Docker/Kubernetes) and ongoing server maintenance.
* **Scalability:** Monday.com scales through automated plan upgrades and centralized cloud resource allocation, whereas Plane's self-hosted scalability is limited entirely by the provisioned hardware and database tuning of your host server.
* **Feature Integration:** Monday.com features a massive native marketplace with hundreds of pre-built business tool integrations (Slack, Salesforce, HubSpot), while Plane focuses primarily on deep, native developer integrations like GitHub, GitLab, and Sentry.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Monday.com | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $9-$19/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | ~$450 - $950/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | ~$1,800 - $3,800/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons

### Monday.com
**Pros:**
* Instant setup with no infrastructure management required
* Extensive native integration marketplace for non-technical tools
* Highly customizable visual boards with multiple views (Kanban, Gantt, Timeline)
* Robust enterprise security features and native compliance certifications
* 24/7 customer support and extensive documentation

**Cons:**
* Costs scale aggressively as team size increases
* Vendor lock-in with proprietary data formats
* Limited depth for software engineering-specific workflows (e.g., cycle planning, git branching)
* Unused user licenses can quietly drive up monthly bills

### Plane
**Pros:**
* 100% free and open-source under the Apache 2.0 license when self-hosted
* Complete data sovereignty and ownership on private infrastructure
* Purpose-built for modern software engineering teams (cycles, modules, issues)
* Fast, keyboard-driven interface optimized for developer speed
* Active open-source community contributing frequent updates

**Cons:**
* Requires technical resources for initial deployment, backups, and updates
* Smaller ecosystem of third-party business integrations compared to Monday.com
* Limited built-in reporting for cross-functional business metrics
* Self-hosted instance support relies primarily on community forums rather than dedicated SLAs

## When to Choose Each
Choose Monday.com if you manage cross-functional business teams—such as marketing, sales, and HR—that require an out-of-the-box, highly visual workspace with zero maintenance overhead. It suits organizations of any size willing to pay for predictable per-user pricing in exchange for enterprise-grade support, deep business app integrations, and guaranteed uptime without internal IT involvement.

Choose Plane if you run software engineering, product, or technical operations teams that prioritize data privacy, custom infrastructure control, and tight integration with developer tools like GitHub. It fits organizations with dedicated DevOps or IT capacity who want to eliminate per-user software licensing fees by hosting their own issue tracking and project management stack.

## Migration Path
1. Export your existing task data, boards, and items from Monday.com into CSV format using the built-in export tool.
2. Set up your target Plane environment via Docker Compose on your private server or cloud infrastructure.
3. Clean and map your Monday.com CSV column headers to match Plane's required import schema (titles, descriptions, states, assignees).
4. Import the mapped CSV data into Plane using the platform's bulk import utility or API scripts.
5. Verify imported issues, cycles, and attachments in Plane, then invite team members to test the new workspace before decommissioning Monday.com.

## Our Take

Plane is production-ready for technical teams comfortable with Docker-based deployments, though it still lacks some of the polished administrative controls and automated audit logs found in mature enterprise SaaS products. Its core issue tracking, cycle management, and modular architecture are stable, fast, and fully capable of replacing traditional tools for engineering-first organizations. However, teams should note one significant technical limitation: self-hosted instances require manual configuration for high-availability database replication and automated backup routines, meaning your internal IT team assumes responsibility for disaster recovery.

Our recommendation is clear. Software-first startups, development agencies, and privacy-conscious tech companies with internal IT capabilities should switch to Plane immediately to eliminate recurring per-user licensing fees. Conversely, non-technical enterprises, large marketing departments, and organizations lacking dedicated infrastructure staff should stay on Monday.com to avoid the hidden maintenance costs of self-hosting.

## Who Should Switch
* A 15-person software startup looking to cut software overhead who do not need CRM or complex financial reporting integrations.
* A 40-person web development agency requiring complete data privacy compliance who do not need client-facing guest billing portals.
* An internal IT department of 8 engineers managing internal tools who do not need out-of-the-box Salesforce or HubSpot connectors.
* A 25-person product team migrating away from Jira who do not need complex enterprise portfolio management hierarchies.
* A bootstrapped SaaS company of 50 developers who do not need multi-tier approval workflows or proprietary cloud hosting.

## FAQ

### Can I migrate my custom boards and automations from Monday.com to Plane?
You can export basic task data and descriptions via CSV, but custom Monday.com automations and complex visual board layouts do not transfer automatically. You will need to recreate your automated workflows and board views natively within Plane after the data import.

### Is Plane really free if I self-host it?
The software itself is open-source and free under the Apache 2.0 license, meaning you pay zero licensing fees regardless of user count. However, you will incur costs for the underlying server infrastructure, storage, and the internal staff time required to maintain and update the deployment.

### Does Plane offer a cloud-hosted version if I don't want to manage my own server?
Yes, Plane offers hosted cloud tiers with managed infrastructure for teams that want the speed of Plane without handling server administration. Pricing for the cloud tier scales based on user count and feature requirements, similar to other SaaS tools.

### How does Plane handle user permissions compared to Monday.com?
Plane provides role-based access control (RBAC) tailored for engineering environments, distinguishing between workspace admins, members, and guests. While sufficient for most software teams, it lacks the hyper-granular item-level and column-level permission restrictions found in Monday.com's enterprise tier.

### Can non-technical teams use Plane effectively?
While Plane's interface is clean and intuitive, it is deliberately engineered around software development methodologies like cycles, milestones, and issues. Non-technical teams like marketing or HR may find its terminology and workflow structures less adaptable than Monday.com's general-purpose visual grids.
meta_description: Plane offers a free, self-hosted alternative to Monday.com for engineering teams. See full comparison and migration guide.
